# Index types — vocabulary

## Terms

### index

- **index** · self — Indexes store references to fields in either ascending (`1`) or descending (`-1`) sort order. For compound indexes, sort order can determine whether the index supports a sort operation. For more information, see [Compound Index Sort Order.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-type · aka: indexes, indices, indexing, indexed — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-compound/#chunk-2

### compound index

- **compound index** · hyponym — Compound indexes may contain **a single** [hashed index field.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed/#std-label-index-type-hashed) · aka: compound indexes, composite index, composite indexes, multi-column index, multicolumn index · MongoDB 'compound' = SQL 'composite'/'multicolumn' — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-compound/#hashed-index-fields

### unique index

- **unique index** · hyponym — Unique indexes ensure that a value appears at most once for a given field. · aka: unique indexes, uniqueIndex — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/create/#chunk-0

### partial index

- **partial index** · hyponym — The `where` argument allows you to define [partial indexes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-partial.html) (also known as filtered indexes). A partial index only includes rows that match a specified condition, which reduces the index size and improves both write performance and query  · aka: partial indexes, filtered index, partialIndexes — https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/v7/prisma-schema/data-model/indexes#configuring-partial-indexes-with-where-configuring-partial-indexes-with-where

### B-tree

- **B-tree** · hyponym — * B-trees are versatile and widely applicable: * **Equality and Range Queries**: They excel in handling equality and range queries. Common operators include `=`, `<`, `>`, `BETWEEN`, and `IN`. * **NULL Conditions**: B-trees can handle `IS NULL` or `IS NOT NULL` conditions. * **Pattern Matching**: Wh · aka: btree, B+tree, b-tree index, B-tree indexes — https://thenile.dev/docs/postgres/indexes#b-tree-index

### GIN index

- **GIN index** · hyponym — * GIN indexes can be large, plan storage accordingly * Index creation might be slow for large tables * Index only necessary columns * Monitor index size and search performance * Adjust similarity threshold to balance precision and recall * Consider using `pg_bigm.enable_recheck` for better accuracy · aka: GIN, GIN indexes, generalized inverted index, gin_trgm_ops · Postgres — https://thenile.dev/docs/extensions/pg_bigm#performance-considerations

### GiST index

- **GiST index** · hyponym — GiST indexes are a versatile type of index that can handle complex data types, such as geometric shapes, full-text search, and network addresses. [They are implemented using a custom data structure optimized for searching large amounts of data1](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/gist.html). He · aka: GiST, SP-GiST, GiST indexes, btree_gist · Postgres — https://thenile.dev/docs/postgres/indexes#gist-index

### BRIN index

- **BRIN index** · hyponym · aka: BRIN, block range index, BRIN indexes · Postgres

### hashed index

- **hashed index** · hyponym — Hashed indexes support [hashed sharding](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/hashed-sharding/#std-label-sharding-hashed-sharding). Hashed indexes index the hash of a field's value. · aka: hashed indexes, hash index, hash indexes, $toHashedIndexKey — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/#chunk-2

### multikey index

- **multikey index** · hyponym — Multikey indexes are used for arrays of values within documents. · aka: multikey, multikey indexes — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ruby-driver/current/llms.txt

### TTL index

- **TTL index** · hyponym · aka: TTL indexes, expireAfterSeconds

### wildcard index

- **wildcard index** · hyponym — Wildcard indexes do not support mixing inclusion and exclusion statements in the `wildcardProjection` document *except* when explicitly including the `_id` field. For more information on `wildcardProjection`, see the [parameter documentation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.c · aka: wildcard indexes — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex/#chunk-32

### geospatial index

- **geospatial index** · hyponym — Geospatial indexes support queries involving location-based data. · aka: geospatial indexes, 2dsphere, 2d index — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ruby-driver/current/llms.txt

### clustered index

- **clustered index** · hyponym — Clustered indexes specify the order in which [clustered collections](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections/#std-label-clustered-collections) store data. Collections created with a clustered index are called clustered collections. · aka: clustered indexes, clustered collection, WITHOUT ROWID — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/#chunk-3

### expression index

- **expression index** · hyponym — An expression index stores the result of an expression rather than a raw column value. Use expression indexes when queries frequently filter or sort by a computed value. · aka: expression indexes, functional index, index on an expression — https://docs.turso.tech/sql-reference/statements/create-index#expression-indexes

### sparse index

- **sparse index** · hyponym · aka: sparse indexes

### hidden index

- **hidden index** · hyponym — - If a hidden index is a [unique index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/#std-label-index-type-unique) , the index still applies its unique constraint to the documents. - If a hidden index is a [TTL index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-ttl/#std-label-index-featu · aka: hidden indexes, hideIndex, unhideIndex — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/#chunk-1

### index definition

- **index definition** · part · aka: index name, index fields, index key, index keys, key pattern, index entry, index entries, index bounds, index specification, IndexFields, IndexName

### index build

### @@index

- **@@index** · instance · aka: @@unique · Prisma schema index attributes

### withIndex

- **withIndex** · instance · aka: IndexRangeBuilder, index range, range expression, .index(, IndexRange, LowerBoundIndexRangeBuilder · Convex index API

### unused index

- **unused index** · problem · aka: unused indexes, redundant index, redundant indexes, duplicate index, index usage, $indexStats, indexStats

### index overhead
